sections.heading: C2 — KG hints for Sign Colors and Shapes
sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for Sign Colors and Shapes

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
Plain yellow warns of general hazards, while fluorescent yellow-green is reserved for pedestrian, bicycle, and school warnings [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec02-F05 and sec02-F06.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
Red commands an action such as stop or yield, while white states the enforceable rule behind such commands [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec02-F02 and sec02-F07.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
Orange marks temporary work-zone conditions, while yellow marks general warnings with no work-zone tie [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec02-F05 and sec02-F08.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A01
Fluorescent pink covers incident response such as crash cleanup and debris removal, while orange covers road work and maintenance [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint sec02-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec02-F08 and sec02-F10.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
Green points the way and blue points to services, while brown points only to recreation and cultural sites [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec02-F03, sec02-F04, and sec02-F09.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A02
The circle warns that a railroad crossing lies ahead, while the crossbuck stands at the crossing itself [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-shapes; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec02-F16 and sec02-F18.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A02
The octagon demands a full stop and the triangle asks only a yield, though both control intersections [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-shapes; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec02-F11 and sec02-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A02
The pennant is a sideways triangle on the left marking no passing, while the diamond is a four-sided warning of hazards [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-shapes; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec02-F14 and sec02-F15.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A02
The rectangle can carry regulatory, guide, or warning messages, while the diamond carries warnings only [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-shapes; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec02-F13 and sec02-F15.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0007]
